rules: P2 DECISION-AUTHORITY.md §3 A1-A9 with the §5 v0.2 changes C1-C5

decisions.statement: The reminder decision in force is DEC-C08 (48 hours before the appointment), not DEC-C06 (24 hours), which DEC-C08 supersedes. `reminders <date>` lists appointments whose appointment date-time minus 48 hours falls on <date>. The requirement's own example (reminders on 2026-03-10 lists appointments on 2026-03-12) agrees.

The existing `reminder <appointment>` command still uses the 24-hour lead (Rules.reminderLeadHours, traced to the superseded DEC-C06) and its existing test expects that. It is left unchanged because CLIN-51 says existing behaviour is unchanged except as its requirements say, and none of them mention `reminder`. The new run list uses a separate DEC-C08 rule (Rules.reminderInForceLeadHours). As a result the two commands disagree on reminder time. Whether `reminder` should move to DEC-C08 is recorded as an open question, not decided here.
Appointments with the same date and time (different clinicians) are ordered by appointment id, as the existing `schedule` command does.
decisions.notAuthorized: Appointments with the same date and time (different clinicians) are ordered by appointment id, as the existing `schedule` command does.
reasons: A6 an `default-rule` decision needs an accepted decision record, a granted approval, or a revision by the owner of every source it changes; requirements of other owners, notes and code cannot authorize it

decisions.statement: <date> is parsed the same way as the other date arguments (yyyy-MM-dd). A malformed date is refused with `error: invalid date <text>`, and a wrong argument count gets `error: usage: reminders <date>`, through the existing error paths. Any date is accepted, past or future, with no horizon check, because nothing restricts it.
`reminders <date>` is added to Cli.usage directly after `reminder <appointment>`. The help output and the usage messages both come from that list.
